articles.title: Bounding number
articles.statement:
The bounding number $\mathfrak{b}$ is the infimum of the cardinalities of
all unbounded families of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Unbounded family
articles.statement:
A family $F$ of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is unbounded if no
function $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ bounds every member of $F$, where $g$ bounds $f$ if there
is an $N$ such that $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all $n \ge N$.

articles.title: Continuum hypothesis
articles.statement: CH: 2^{ℵ₀}=ℵ₁

articles.title: Equivalent forms of the continuum hypothesis
articles.statement:
1. The continuum hypothesis holds if and only if the continuum equals ℵ₁.   2. The continuum
   hypothesis holds if and only if the continuum is at most ℵ₁.   3. The continuum hypothesis holds
   if and only if the reals have cardinality ℵ₁, i.e. |ℝ| =      ℵ₁.   4. The continuum hypothesis
   holds if and only if there is no cardinal strictly between ℵ₀ and the continuum.   5.

The full informal statement is in the module documentation directly above.

articles.title: Singular cardinals hypothesis
articles.statement:
For all singular cardinal $\kappa$, if $2^{cof(\kappa)}\lt \kappa, then $\kappa^{cof(\kappa)} =
\kappa^+$.

articles.title: Cofinal type
articles.statement:
A cofinal type is an equivalence class of preordered sets under Tukey
equivalence $\equiv_T$, where $D \equiv_T E$ means $D \le_T E$ and $E \le_T D$ (Tukey
reducibility in both directions).

articles.title: Tukey equivalence
articles.statement:
Preordered sets $D$ and $E$ are Tukey equivalent (cofinally
equivalent), written $D \equiv_T E$, if $D \le_T E$ and $E \le_T D$, where $\le_T$ is Tukey
reducibility.

articles.title: Tukey reducibility
articles.statement:
For preordered sets $D$ and $E$, $D$ is Tukey reducible to $E$,
written $D \le_T E$, if there is a map $f \colon D \to E$ that carries unbounded sets to
unbounded sets: for every $A \subseteq D$ with no upper bound in $D$, the image $f[A]$ has no
upper bound in $E$.

articles.title: Countable chain condition
articles.statement:
A partial order $(P, \le)$ has the countable chain condition
(c.c.c.) if every antichain of $P$ is countable, where an antichain is a set of pairwise
incompatible elements: no two distinct members of it have a common lower bound in $P$.

articles.title: σ-centered partial orders
articles.statement:
A partial order $P$ is $\sigma$-centered if there is a map
$c : P \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every finite set of elements $p$
with $c(p) = n$ has a common lower bound in $P$. Thus $P$ splits into countably many centered
pieces $c^{-1}(n)$; the empty set is among the finite sets, so $P$ must be nonempty.

articles.title: Martin's axiom for σ-centered partial orders
articles.statement:
For a cardinal $\kappa$, this is the
statement that for every $\sigma$-centered partial order $P$, every family $\mathcal{D}$ of at
most $\kappa$ dense subsets of $P$ and every $p \in P$, there is a filter $G$ on $P$ with
$p \in G$ that meets every member of $\mathcal{D}$. Here $D \subseteq P$ is dense if every
element of $P$ has an element of $D$ below it, and a filter is a nonempty upward closed subset
of $P$ any two of whose elements have a common lower bound in it.

articles.title: Martin's axiom
articles.statement:
For a cardinal $\kappa$, $\mathrm{MA}(\kappa)$ is the statement that for
every partial order $P$ with the countable chain condition, every family $\mathcal{D}$ of at most
$\kappa$ dense subsets of $P$ and every $p \in P$, there is a filter $G$ on $P$ with $p \in G$
that meets every member of $\mathcal{D}$. Here $D \subseteq P$ is dense if every element of $P$
has an element of $D$ below it, and a filter is a nonempty upward closed subset of $P$ any two
of whose elements have a common lower bound in it.

articles.title: Free set for a coloring
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a set and $K \subseteq X \times X$. A set
$H \subseteq X$ is $K$-free if $(x, y) \notin K$ for all $x, y \in H$.

articles.title: Homogeneous set for a coloring
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a set and $K \subseteq X \times X$. A set
$H \subseteq X$ is $K$-homogeneous if $(x, y) \in K$ for all distinct $x, y \in H$.

articles.title: Open coloring of a topological space
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space. A set
$K \subseteq X \times X$ of ordered pairs is an open coloring of $X$ if $K$ is open in the
product topology, symmetric ($(x, y) \in K$ implies $(y, x) \in K$) and irreflexive
($(x, x) \notin K$ for every $x \in X$).

articles.title: Open coloring axiom
articles.statement:
Todorcevic's Open Coloring Axiom: for every open coloring of a second-countable space,
either there is an uncountable homogeneous set, or the space is a countable union of free sets.

articles.title: Orthogonality to a family of sets
articles.statement:
Let $I$ be a family of subsets of a set $\alpha$. A
set $X \subseteq \alpha$ is orthogonal to $I$ if $X \cap a$ is finite for every $a \in I$.

articles.title: P-ideal of countable sets
articles.statement:
A family $I$ of subsets of a set $\alpha$ is a P-ideal of
countable sets if every member of $I$ is countable, every subset of a member of $I$ is in $I$,
every finite subset of $\alpha$ is in $I$, $I$ is closed under binary unions, and for every
sequence $(a_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of members of $I$ there is $b \in I$ with $a_n \subseteq^* b$
(that is, $a_n \setminus b$ is finite) for every $n$.

articles.title: P-ideal dichotomy
articles.statement:
The P-ideal dichotomy (PID): for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of an uncountable
set, either some uncountable set has all its countable subsets in I, or the whole set is a
countable union of sets orthogonal to I.

articles.title: Inclusion modulo finite
articles.statement:
For subsets $a$ and $b$ of a set $\alpha$, $a \subseteq^* b$
($a$ is almost contained in $b$) if the difference $a \setminus b$ is finite.

articles.title: Compatible conditions
articles.statement:
Two elements $p$ and $q$ of a partial order $\mathbb{P}$ are
compatible if there is $r \in \mathbb{P}$ with $r \le p$ and $r \le q$.

articles.title: (M, ℙ)-generic conditions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a partial order and $M$ a subset of the
disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. Write $M_c$ for the set of
$p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union lies in $M$, and $M_s$ for the set of
$D \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ whose copy lies in $M$. A condition $q \in \mathbb{P}$ is
$(M, \mathbb{P})$-generic if for every $D \in M_s$ that is dense in $\mathbb{P}$ (every element
of $\mathbb{P}$ has an element of $D$ below it), the set $D \cap M_c$ is predense below $q$: for
every $r \le q$ there are $a \in D \cap M_c$ and $s \in \mathbb{P}$ with $s \le r$ and $s \le a$.

No condition is imposed on $M$ here. In the intended application $M$ is the trace of a countable
elementary submodel of $H(\theta)$, for a sufficiently large regular cardinal $\theta$, that
contains $\mathbb{P}$; genericity depends only on $M_c$ and $M_s$, and the elementarity is
supplied by the club in the definition of proper partial orders.

articles.title: Predense below a condition
articles.statement:
A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ of elements of a partial order
$\mathbb{P}$ is predense below $q \in \mathbb{P}$ if for every $r \le q$ there is $a \in A$ such
that $r$ and $a$ are compatible.

articles.title: Proper partial orders
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a partial order and let $X$ be the disjoint
union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$; for $M \subseteq X$ write $M_c$ for the set of
$p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in $X$ lies in $M$. Then $\mathbb{P}$ is proper if there is a club
$C$ in $[X]^\omega$ such that for every $M \in C$ and every $p \in M_c$ there is an
$(M, \mathbb{P})$-generic condition $q \le p$. Here a club in $[X]^\omega$ is a family of
countable subsets of $X$ such that every countable subset of $X$ is contained in a member of the
family, and the union of every increasing sequence $M_0 \subseteq M_1 \subseteq \cdots$ of
members of the family is again a member.

The usual requirement $\mathbb{P} \in M$ is not imposed: $\mathbb{P}$ is an element of $X$ (as a
subset of itself), and since $C$ is cofinal it has members containing it.

articles.title: Conditions in a model
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a set and $M$ a subset of the disjoint union
$\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. The conditions in $M$ form the set $M_c$ of those
$p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union belongs to $M$; informally,
$M_c = M \cap \mathbb{P}$.

articles.title: Sets of conditions in a model
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a set and $M$ a subset of the disjoint
union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. The sets of conditions in $M$ form the family
$M_s$ of those $D \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union belongs to $M$;
informally, $M_s = M \cap \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$.

articles.title: Proper Forcing Axiom
articles.statement:
For every proper partial order $\mathbb{P}$, every family
$\mathcal{D}$ of at most $\aleph_1$ dense subsets of $\mathbb{P}$, and every condition
$p \in \mathbb{P}$, there is a filter $G \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ with $p \in G$ that meets every
member of $\mathcal{D}$, that is, $G \cap D \neq \emptyset$ for every $D \in \mathcal{D}$.

Here a set $D \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ is dense if for every $q \in \mathbb{P}$ there is $d \in D$
with $d \le q$, and a filter is a nonempty, upward closed subset $G$ of $\mathbb{P}$ such that
any two elements of $G$ have a common lower bound in $G$.

articles.title: Almost disjoint family of functions on a regular cardinal
articles.statement:
Let κ be a regular cardinal. A family of functions κ → κ is *almost disjoint* if for all f and g
in the family with f≠ g, |{ α ∣ f(α ) = g(α ) }|<κ..

articles.title: Functions almost disjoint modulo the nonstationary ideal
articles.statement:
Functions f, g ∈ ∏_{α<ω₁} A_α are *almost disjoint mod the nonstationary ideal* if the set {  α
< ω₁ : f(α) = g(α)  } on which they agree is nonstationary in ω₁.

articles.title: $\kappa$-almost disjoint family of sets
articles.statement:
A family F ⊆ 𝒫(I) is *κ-almost disjoint* if |A| = κ for every A ∈ F and |A ∩ B| < κ for all
distinct A, B ∈ F.

articles.title: Aronszajn tree
articles.statement:
An *Aronszajn tree* is a tree of height $\aleph_1}$ all of whose levels are at most countable
and which has no uncountable branches.

articles.title: $\kappa$-Aronszajn tree
articles.statement: A κ-Aronszajn tree is a κ-tree such that there are no cofinal branch through the tree.

articles.title: $\omega_1$-tree
articles.statement:
An *ω₁-tree* is a tree of height ω₁ all of whose levels are countable: every node has height <
ω₁, every level Lev_α(T) with α < ω₁ is nonempty, and every such level is countable.

articles.title: Partial order that is a union of countably many antichains
articles.statement:
A partial order (P, ≤) is a *union of ω antichains* if P = ⋃_{n<ω} Aₙ where each Aₙ ⊆ P is an
antichain (a set of pairwise ≤-incomparable elements).

articles.title: Special partial order
articles.statement:
A partial order (α,≤) is *special* if there is a map
f : α → ℚ that is strictly increasing, i.e.\
x < y implies f(x) < f(y).  Note that f need not be injective:
nothing is required of incomparable elements.

articles.title: $\kappa$-Suslin tree
articles.statement: A κ-Suslin tree is a κ-Aronszajn tree with no antichains of size κ.

articles.title: Suslin tree
articles.statement:
A *Suslin tree* is a tree of height $\aleph_1}$ with no uncountable branches and no uncountable
antichains.

articles.title: Level of a well-founded partial order
articles.statement:
For an ordinal α, the *α-th level* of a well-founded partial order (T, <) is Lev_α(T) = {  x ∈ T
: ht(x) = α  }, the set of elements whose height equals α.

articles.title: Normal tree at a cardinal
Tree (set theory)
articles.statement:
A *tree* is a partially ordered set (T, <) iwith the property that for each x ∈ T, the set {  y
∈ T : y < x  } of all predecessors of x is well-ordered by <).

articles.title: Equality modulo finite sets
articles.statement:
Subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\mathbb{N}$ are *equal modulo finite*,
written $A =^{\ast} B$, if their symmetric difference $A \mathbin{\triangle} B$ is finite.

articles.title: Automorphisms of P(ω)/fin on representatives
articles.statement:
For subsets $A$, $B$ of $\mathbb{N}$, write
$A =^{\ast} B$ when their symmetric difference is finite. A map $\Phi$ from subsets of
$\mathbb{N}$ to subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ presents an automorphism of $P(\omega)/\mathrm{fin}$ if for
all subsets $A$, $B$ of $\mathbb{N}$: it respects $=^{\ast}$ ($A =^{\ast} B$ implies
$\Phi(A) =^{\ast} \Phi(B)$), it preserves meets ($\Phi(A \cap B) =^{\ast} \Phi(A) \cap \Phi(B)$)
and complements ($\Phi(\mathbb{N} \setminus A) =^{\ast} \mathbb{N} \setminus \Phi(A)$), it is
one-to-one modulo finite ($\Phi(A) =^{\ast} \Phi(B)$ implies $A =^{\ast} B$), and it is onto
modulo finite (for every $B$ there is $A$ with $\Phi(A) =^{\ast} B$).

articles.title: Closure points and clubs of countable subsets
articles.statement:
1. Let F : Finset(α) → α. Then ClosurePointsSeq(λ n : ℕ,, F) =      ClosurePoints(F).   2. For
   every finitary operation F, ∅ ∉ ClosurePoints(F).   3. Let f : ℕ → 𝒫(α) with each f(n) countable.
   Then ⋃_{n ∈ ℕ} f(n)      is countable.   4. [α]^ω is club in [α]^ω.   5. ∅ is not stationary in
   [α]^ω.   6. If S is stationary in [α]^ω then S ≠ ∅.   7.

The full informal statement is in the module documentation directly above.

articles.title: Closure points of a sequence of finitary functions
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a set and let
$(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions, each assigning an element of $X$ to every
finite subset of $X$. The closure points of $(F_n)$ are the countable (finite or countably
infinite) sets $x \subseteq X$ such that $F_n(s) \in x$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
finite set $s \subseteq x$.

articles.title: Closure points of a finitary function
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a set and let $F$ be a function
assigning an element of $X$ to every finite subset of $X$. The closure points of $F$ are the
countable (finite or countably infinite) sets $a \subseteq X$ such that $F(s) \in a$ for every
finite set $s \subseteq a$.

articles.title: Club subset of $P_\kappa(\lambda)$
articles.statement:
C ⊆ P_κ(λ) is club iff

1. C is ⊆-cofinal: ∀ x ∈ P_κ(λ)  ∃ y ∈ C  (x ⊆ y), and
1. C is closed under unions of nonempty ⊆-directed subfamilies of size < κ: for every nonempty
   ⊆-directed D ⊆ C with |D| < κ, ⋃ D ∈ C.

articles.title: Countable subsets of a set
articles.statement: [α]^ω or P_{ω₁}(α) is the set of countable subsets of α

articles.title: Family containing all bounded subsets of a cardinal
articles.statement:
A set X⊆κ is *bounded in κ* if there is some
β<κ with α<β for every α∈ X; equivalently,
X⊆β for some β<κ.

A family I⊆𝒫(κ) *contains all bounded sets*
if every bounded X⊆κ belongs to I:

∀ X ⊆ κ  [
    (∃ β < κ ∀ α ∈ X, α < β)
     ⟶  X ∈ I
   ].

articles.title: Club families of countable sets
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a set. A family $C$ of subsets of $X$ is club
in the countable subsets of $X$ when every member of $C$ is countable (finite or countably
infinite), every countable set $x \subseteq X$ is contained in some member of $C$, and for every
sequence $x_0 \subseteq x_1 \subseteq x_2 \subseteq \cdots$ of members of $C$ the union
$\bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} x_n$ belongs to $C$.

articles.title: Regressive functions
articles.statement:
Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal, identified with its initial ordinal, let
$S$ be a set of ordinals less than $\kappa$, and let $f$ be a function from $S$ to the ordinals
less than $\kappa$. Then $f$ is regressive if $f(\alpha) < \alpha$ for every nonzero
$\alpha \in S$.

articles.title: Stationary families of countable sets
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a set. A family $S$ of subsets of $X$ is
stationary in the countable subsets of $X$ when $S$ meets every family $C$ that is club in the
countable subsets of $X$, that is, some set belongs to both $S$ and $C$.

articles.title: $\kappa$-complete ideal on a cardinal
articles.statement:
A *κ-complete ideal on κ* is a collection I ⊆ 𝒫(κ) such that:

1. ∅ ∈ I.
1. If A ∈ I and B ⊆ A, then B ∈ I.
1. κ ∉ I.
1. If λ < κ and ⟨ A_α : α < λ ⟩ is a sequence of members of I, then [ ⋃_{α < λ} A_α ∈ I. ]

articles.title: Normal ideal on a cardinal
articles.statement:
Let κ be a cardinal, identified with
κ = Iio(κ.ord) = {α : Ordinal ∣ α < κ.ord},
and let I⊆𝒫(κ).

I is *normal* if it is closed under diagonal unions: for every
κ-sequence ⟨ A_ξ : ξ<κ⟩ with A_ξ∈ I,

∇_{ξ<κ} A_ξ := {α<κ ∣ ∃ ξ<α, α∈ A_ξ} ∈ I.

Formally,

∀ A : κ → 𝒫(κ),  (∀ ξ, A_ξ∈ I) →
  {α∈κ ∣ ∃ ξ∈κ, ξ<α ∧ α∈ A_ξ}∈ I.

articles.title: Subsets of $\lambda$ of size less than $\kappa$
Diamond-minus principle
articles.statement:
◇⁻_κ holds iff there is a sequence ⟨ 𝒜_α : α < κ⟩ with each 𝒜_α ⊆ 𝒫(α) and |𝒜_α| ≤ |α|, such
that for every X ⊆ κ the set {α < κ : X ∩ α ∈ 𝒜_α} is stationary in κ.

articles.title: Diamond principle
articles.statement:
◇_κ holds iff there is a sequence ⟨ S_α : α < κ⟩ with S_α ⊆ α for all α < κ, such that for every
X ⊆ κ, {α < κ : X ∩ α = S_α} is stationary in κ.

articles.title: Δ-system
articles.statement:
A family $A$ of subsets of a type $\alpha$ is a Δ-system with root
$r \subseteq \alpha$ if $s \cap t = r$ for any two distinct members $s$ and $t$ of $A$.

articles.title: Ramsey ultrafilter
articles.statement:
An ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ is *Ramsey* if for every sequence
$(A_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of pairwise disjoint subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ whose union is
$\mathbb{N}$ and such that $A_n \notin U$ for all $n$, there is $X \in U$ such that
$X \cap A_n$ has at most one element for every $n$.

articles.title: Shelah's theorem (Erdős Problem 1219)
articles.statement:
For every strictly increasing sequence
$n_0 < n_1 < \cdots$ of natural numbers such that the cardinals $2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ are strictly
increasing in $k$ and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$, the partition relation
$\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2_2$ holds: for every set $X$ of cardinality
$\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ and every symmetric colouring of the pairs of elements of $X$ with two
colours, some subset of $X$ of cardinality $\aleph_\omega$ has all pairs of distinct elements of
the same colour.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #1219, https://www.erdosproblems.com/1219 (status PROVED); resolution: S. Shelah, Notes on partition calculus, in Infinite and Finite Sets (Colloq. Keszthely, 1973), Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 10, North-Holland (1975), 1257-1276, erdosproblems.com/1219: proved by Shelah (a problem of Erdős, Hajnal and Rado; P. Komjáth, The Erdős-Hajnal problem list, Bull. Symb. Log. (2025), p. 2).

articles.title: Erdős Problem 1219: a partition relation for sums of powers of two
articles.statement:
The statement that for
every strictly increasing sequence $n_0 < n_1 < \cdots$ of natural numbers such that the cardinals
$2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ are strictly increasing in $k$ and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$, the
partition relation $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2_2$ holds: for every set $X$ of
cardinality $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ and every symmetric colouring of the pairs of elements of $X$
with two colours, some subset of $X$ of cardinality $\aleph_\omega$ has all pairs of distinct
elements of the same colour.

articles.title: Partition relation for pairs with two colours
articles.statement:
For cardinals $\kappa$ and $\mu$, the
relation $\kappa \to (\mu)^2_2$ holds if for every set $X$ of cardinality $\kappa$ and every
symmetric colouring $c$ of the ordered pairs of elements of $X$ with two colours, there are a
subset $H \subseteq X$ of cardinality $\mu$ and a colour $b$ such that $c(x, y) = b$ for all
distinct $x, y \in H$.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 591 is true
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$. For every red/blue colouring of
the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$, that is, every pair of
complementary simple graphs (red and blue) on this set, there is a red clique whose order type
is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation,
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.

## Sources

- Schipperus [Sc10] and Darby, independently, per erdosproblems.com/591, https://www.erdosproblems.com/591.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 591
articles.statement:
The statement that, for $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$, every red/blue
colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ (that is, every
pair of complementary simple graphs, red and blue, on this set) has a red clique whose order
type is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation,
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.

articles.title: Homogeneous set
articles.statement:
Let $c$ assign a colour in $\gamma$ to each finite subset of a type
$I$, and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $H \subseteq I$ is homogeneous for $c$ with colour
$k \in \gamma$ if $c(s) = k$ for every $n$-element subset $s$ of $H$.

Only the values of $c$ on $n$-element sets matter, so $c$ plays the role of a colouring
$[I]^n \to \gamma$ of the $n$-element subsets of $I$.

articles.title: Ordinal–cardinal Ramsey property
articles.statement:
For ordinals $\alpha$, $\beta$ and a cardinal $c$, the
partition property $\alpha \to (\beta, c)^2$ holds if for every coloring of the edges of the
complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ in red and blue, either some set of vertices
whose order type is $\beta$ has all its edges red, or some set of vertices of cardinality exactly
$c$ has all its edges blue.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 118 fails for ordinals
articles.statement:
There exist an ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying the partition
relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and a natural number $n \ge 3$ such that $\alpha$ does not
satisfy $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.

Schipperus and Darby independently answered the question in the negative. A concrete
counterexample is $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$ with $n = 5$: Schipperus proved
$\omega^{\omega^\beta} \to (\omega^{\omega^\beta}, 3)^2$ when $\beta$ is a sum of two additively
indecomposable ordinals (here $\beta = 1 + 1$), and Larson proved
$\omega^{\omega^\beta} \not\to (\omega^{\omega^\beta}, 5)^2$ for every $\beta$ that is not
additively indecomposable.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #118, https://www.erdosproblems.com/118 (status DISPROVED); resolution: R. Schipperus, Countable partition ordinals, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 161 (2010), 1195-1215; C. Darby, Negative partition relations for ordinals ω^{ω^α}, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 76 (1999), 205-222; J. A. Larson, An ordinal partition avoiding pentagrams, J. Symbolic Logic 65 (2000), 969-978, erdosproblems.com/118: answered no independently by Schipperus and Darby; for α = ω^{ω²}: ω^{ω²} → (ω^{ω²}, 3)² (Schipperus: ω^{ω^β} → (ω^{ω^β}, 3)² when β is a sum of two additively indecomposable ordinals) and ω^{ω²} ↛ (ω^{ω²}, 5)² (Larson, main theorem: ω^{ω^β} ↛ (ω^{ω^β}, 5)² for β not additively indecomposable; zbMATH 0967.03042); Hajnal-Larson, Handbook of Set Theory, Chapter 2.9.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 118 for ordinals
articles.statement:
The statement that for every ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying
the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and every natural number $n \ge 3$, the ordinal
$\alpha$ also satisfies $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.

articles.title: Ordinal partition relation
articles.statement:
For an ordinal $\alpha$ and a natural number $n$, the partition
relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$ holds when every colouring of the pairs $x < y$ of ordinals
below $\alpha$ in red and blue has a red set of order type $\alpha$ or a blue set of size $n$:
either there is a strictly increasing map $f$ from the ordinals below $\alpha$ to the ordinals
below $\alpha$ such that the pair $\{f(x), f(y)\}$ is red for all $x < y < \alpha$, or there is a
set of $n$ ordinals below $\alpha$ all of whose pairs are blue.

articles.title: Jensen's square principle
articles.statement: □_κ: a □_κ-sequence exists

articles.title: Square sequence
articles.statement:
Jensen's square principle sequence:  C = (C_α : α < κ⁺) is a □_κ-sequence: for every limit
 α < κ⁺, C_α is club in α of order type at most κ, and the family coheres —
 C_β = C_α ∩ β whenever β is a limit point of C_α.

articles.title: A regular beth fixed point is inaccessible
articles.statement:
Converse to `IsInaccessible.beth_ord`: a regular beth fixed point is
inaccessible.  Uncountability is derived, not assumed
(`aleph0_lt_of_isRegular_beth_ord`); for `x < κ`,
`2 ^ x ≤ 2 ^ ℶ_{x.ord} = ℶ_{succ x.ord} < κ`, using that `κ.ord` is a limit
ordinal.

Regularity is genuinely needed — the first beth fixed point is singular — so
this does not promote a bare fixed point.

## Sources

- A regular beth fixed point is inaccessible.

articles.title: A regular beth fixed point is uncountable
articles.statement:
A regular beth fixed point is uncountable: regularity gives `ℵ₀ ≤ κ`, and
`κ = ℵ₀` fails the fixed-point equation since `ℶ_ω > ℶ_0 = ℵ₀`.

## Sources

- A regular beth fixed point is uncountable.

articles.title: At most $\kappa$ inaccessible cardinals lie below $\kappa$
articles.statement:
There are at most `κ` inaccessibles below `κ`: the set injects into
`↥(Set.Iio κ.ord)`, which has size `lift κ`.  The `≤` half of the counting needed
for the Mahlo-implies-fixed-point benchmark item.

The `lift` is forced: the carrier lives in `Type (u+1)`, the same phenomenon as
the `lift` in `IsInaccessibleFixedPoint`.

## Sources

- There are at most κ inaccessible cardinals below κ.

articles.title: Exactly $\kappa$ inaccessibles lie below an inaccessible fixed point
articles.statement:
The fixed-point equation forces `#(inaccessibleBelow κ) = lift κ`
(`card_type`): the companion to the upper bound `mk_inaccessibleBelow_le`.

## Sources

- Below an inaccessible fixed point κ there are exactly κ inaccessible cardinals.

articles.title: Existence of an inaccessible with no inaccessibles below it
articles.statement:
If any inaccessible exists, some inaccessible has no inaccessibles below it:
minimize over the initial ordinals of inaccessible cardinals
(`WellFounded.has_min`), and any member of `inaccessibleBelow` would give a
smaller one.

In particular the least inaccessible — if one exists — is neither Mahlo (see
`exists_isInaccessible_not_isMahlo` in `Mahlo.lean`) nor an inaccessible fixed
point (`not_isInaccessibleFixedPoint_of_inaccessibleBelow_eq_empty` above).

## Sources

- If any inaccessible cardinal exists, some inaccessible has no inaccessibles below it.

articles.title: Inaccessible cardinals are the regular beth fixed points
articles.statement:
`κ` is inaccessible iff it is regular and a beth fixed point (uncountability
is automatic by `aleph0_lt_of_isRegular_beth_ord`): this packages
`of_isRegular_beth_ord` with Mathlib's `IsInaccessible.beth_ord`.

## Sources

- κ is inaccessible if and only if κ is regular and a beth fixed point.

articles.title: Inaccessible fixed point
articles.statement:
A cardinal κ is an *inaccessible fixed point* if κ is inaccessible and the inaccessibles below κ
have order type κ (i.e. κ is the κ-th inaccessible).

articles.title: Inaccessibles are unbounded below an inaccessible fixed point
articles.statement:
Inaccessibles below an inaccessible fixed point are unbounded: if they were
bounded by `a`, the set would inject into `Iic a.val`, hence have size at most
`lift (a.val + 1).card < lift κ` — contradicting `mk_inaccessibleBelow`.

## Sources

- Inaccessibles below an inaccessible fixed point are unbounded.

articles.title: Limit cardinals are unbounded below a weakly inaccessible cardinal
articles.statement:
Limit cardinals are unbounded below a weakly inaccessible `κ`: the sup of
the `ω`-chain `μ 0 = succ (max a ℵ₀)`, `μ (n+1) = succ (μ n)` stays below `κ`
(`sum_lt_of_isRegular`), exceeds `a`, and is a limit since every `x < σ`
lies below some `μ n` (`exists_lt_of_lt_ciSup`).

## Sources

- Above any a < κ with κ weakly inaccessible sits a limit cardinal below κ.

articles.title: Regular cardinals are unbounded below an uncountable limit cardinal
articles.statement:
Regular cardinals are unbounded below an uncountable limit cardinal `κ` (in
particular a weakly inaccessible one): above any `a < κ` sits
`succ (max a ℵ₀)`, regular by `isRegular_succ` and below `κ` since `κ` is a
limit.

## Sources

- Regular cardinals are unbounded below any uncountable limit cardinal.

articles.title: Set of inaccessible cardinals below a cardinal
articles.statement: InAccBelow κ is the set of all inaccessible cardinals below κ.

articles.title: Set of regular cardinals below a cardinal
articles.statement:
The **regular cardinals below `κ`**, carried as initial ordinals — parallel to
`inaccessibleBelow`, and definitionally the stationary set in `IsWeaklyMahlo`.
Spelled with Mathlib's `Ordinal.IsInitial`.

## Sources

- regularBelow κ is the set of initial ordinals below κ whose cardinals are regular.

articles.title: Strong limit cardinals are closed under exponentiation
articles.statement:
A strong limit `κ` is closed under cardinal exponentiation: `x ^ y ≤ 2 ^ (x * y)`
(via `cantor` and `power_mul`), and `x * y < κ` by `mul_lt_of_lt`.  No
infiniteness hypothesis is needed — it is automatic by `IsStrongLimit.aleph0_le`.

## Sources

- Below a strong limit κ, x < κ and y < κ imply x ^ y < κ.

articles.title: Strong limits are unbounded below an inaccessible cardinal
articles.statement:
Strong limits are unbounded below an inaccessible `κ`: above any `a < κ` sits
`ℶ_{a.ord + ω}`, a strong limit by `isStrongLimit_beth` since `a.ord + ω` is a
limit ordinal (`isSuccLimit_add`), and below `κ` since
`(a.ord + ω).card = a.ord.card + ℵ₀ < κ` (`add_lt_of_lt`).

## Sources

- Above any a < κ with κ inaccessible sits a strong limit cardinal below κ.

articles.title: Supremum of a bounded set of initial ordinals is initial
articles.statement:
The sup of a bounded set of initial ordinals is initial: if
`σ.card.ord < σ` then some member exceeds `σ.card.ord`, trapping it strictly
between itself and its own initial ordinal.

## Sources

- The supremum of a bounded set of initial ordinals is initial.

articles.title: The aleph hierarchy stays below an inaccessible cardinal
articles.statement:
Below an inaccessible `κ`, the aleph hierarchy stays below `κ`: same argument
via `IsInaccessible.aleph_ord`.

## Sources

- Below an inaccessible κ, each ℵ_o with o < κ.ord lies below κ.

articles.title: The beth hierarchy stays below an inaccessible cardinal
articles.statement:
Below an inaccessible `κ`, the beth hierarchy stays below `κ`: `κ` is a beth
fixed point (`IsInaccessible.beth_ord`) and `beth` is strictly monotone.

## Sources

- Below an inaccessible κ, each ℶ_o with o < κ.ord lies below κ.

articles.title: Under GCH, weakly inaccessible cardinals are inaccessible
articles.statement:
Under (local) GCH, weakly inaccessible implies strongly inaccessible: for
infinite `μ < κ`, `2 ^ μ = succ μ < κ` by the limit property, and the finite
case is `power_lt_aleph0`.

`GCH` is spelled inline and localized below `κ`, following the
`singularCardinalsHypothesis_of_gch` precedent (Mathlib has no `GCH` identifier);
the `ℵ₀ ≤ μ` restriction is load-bearing for the same reason as there.

## Sources

- Under GCH below κ, a weakly inaccessible κ is inaccessible.

articles.title: Weak power below a strong limit cardinal equals the cardinal
articles.statement:
For `2 ≤ x < κ` with `κ` a strong limit, `x ^< κ = κ`: every smaller power is
below `κ` (`IsStrongLimit.power_lt`), while every `y < κ` sits below
`2 ^ y ≤ x ^< κ`.  No infiniteness hypothesis is needed — it is automatic by
`IsStrongLimit.aleph0_le`.

## Sources

- For 2 ≤ x < κ with κ a strong limit, x ^< κ = κ.

articles.title: Weakly inaccessible cardinal
articles.statement: A cardinal κ is *weakly inaccessible* if it is an uncountable, regular limit cardinal.

articles.title: Weakly compact cardinal
articles.statement:
A cardinal $\kappa$ is *weakly compact* if $\aleph_0 < \kappa$
and $\kappa \to (\kappa)^2_2$: for every set $I$ of cardinality $\kappa$ and every colouring $c$
of the finite subsets of $I$ with two colours, there are a subset $H \subseteq I$ of cardinality
$\kappa$ and a colour $k$ such that $c(s) = k$ for every two-element subset $s \subseteq H$.

articles.title: Mahlo cardinal
articles.statement:
A cardinal κ is *Mahlo* if κ is inaccessible and the set {  λ < κ : λ  is inaccessible  } of
inaccessibles below κ is stationary in κ.

articles.title: Weakly Mahlo cardinal
articles.statement:
A cardinal κ is *weakly Mahlo* if κ is weakly inaccessible and {  λ < κ : λ  is a regular
cardinal  } is stationary in κ.

articles.title: Measurable cardinal
articles.statement:
A cardinal κ is *measurable* if κ > ℵ₀ and there is a
set I with |I| = κ carrying an ultrafilter U on I which is

1. *κ-complete*: for every family 𝒮 ⊆ U with |𝒮| < κ we have ⋂ 𝒮 ∈ U; and
1. *nonprincipal*: every cofinite subset of I belongs to U --- equivalently, since U is an
   ultrafilter, no finite subset of I belongs to U.
